# Customer contact access and retention

- Entry ID: product/customer-contact-retention
- Researched: 5 November 2026
- Status: approved and implemented at the HTTP route boundary; final verification is recorded below. The founder additionally requires ACTIVE registration before full profiles and detailed reviews. Production provider controllers remain planned.
- Question: should CEREMO require registration before releasing provider contacts, and what creates repeat use after the first introduction?
- Scope: provider-subscription discovery marketplace in Greater Accra; customer registration remains free, outside conversations and service payments remain permitted. No commission, escrow or service checkout is proposed.

## Local context and correction

The original research and alternatives below preceded implementation. The founder's later approval extends the contact proposal to full profiles and detailed reviews. Follow [ADR 11.10](../../../docs/03-technical-requirements.md#1110-registered-profile-and-contact-access) and the implementation record below where the original proposal differs.

The founder challenged the previous recommendation to publish provider contacts without an account. That recommendation followed the current PRD/journeys but did not adequately assess Ghanaian contact-gating precedents. Jiji Ghana provides direct evidence of a registration gate for contact details. The earlier [registration timing review](../application/customer-lifecycle.md#registration-timing-review-5-november-2026) is therefore superseded as a recommendation about contact access. Its public-browsing/no-timer recommendation remains useful. Existing public-contact requirements require an explicit coordinated revision before implementation; this register does not silently change them.

Two separate hypotheses need testing: a contact gate creates more reachable registered accounts; useful account features make those people return. A gate alone cannot establish the second hypothesis. Once a business number is disclosed, a customer can retain it or find it elsewhere. CEREMO's provider-subscription revenue model does not require every subsequent service transaction to take place on CEREMO.

## Evidence register

All sources reviewed on 5 November 2026. These are published policies/help pages or public product pages, not competitor source code or authenticated end-to-end tests. No account, message, call, subscription or interview was created. No company material was submitted to a third party. No source implementation was copied, so no software licence/dependency import applies.

| --- | --- | --- |

It does not prove increased retention, conversion or technical enforcement across every client. Jiji's other collection practices are not proposed for CEREMO. |

Some customer numbers can be revealed; calls can use masked numbers. | Stronger control is possible but carries inbox/telephony operating cost. Search results and community anecdotes do not establish a universal senior-engineering practice. No suitable public competitor Spring backend implementation was identified or needed for this product decision. No inaccessible Slack/LinkedIn claims or unverifiable engineer credentials are used.

## Alternatives and recommended flow

| Option | Benefit | Cost/risk | Recommendation |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Public business contacts | Lowest contact friction | Visitors can leave without an account; limited account-linked follow-up | Supersede the previous recommendation after the founder's challenge. Retain as a possible research comparator only if approved. |
| Free active account before contact | Account-linked contact action, clearer repeat-use opportunity, modest implementation scope | Registration/verification can lose useful contacts; numbers can be retained afterwards | Recommended first policy to validate. |
| Mandatory internal messaging before sharing details | More interaction stays observable in the product | Inbox delivery/moderation/notification operations and duplicate-channel burden | Later option only if real customer/provider research justifies it. |
| Masked calls and enforced off-platform restrictions | More controlled communication | Telephony cost, call quality/trust/privacy work; poor fit with permitted outside contact | Not recommended for the current MVP. |

Recommended journey: browse profiles/reviews free -> choose Contact provider -> explain free account requirement -> sign in/register through existing Keycloak flow -> verified-email ACTIVE account -> return to chosen provider -> deliberately select call, WhatsApp or a structured enquiry. No elapsed-time restriction, mandatory survey or full event plan. Returning active accounts should not register again; authentication/session policy is separate. Do not invent a numeric contact quota.

Recheck provider publication, accepting-contact state, relevant service and current trial/subscription entitlement at contact release. A suspended provider cannot regain contact eligibility by paying. Contact opening/reveal is not a conversation, enquiry, hire or completed service. Do not silently send the customer's phone or event brief to a provider when the person merely reveals a number. Structured enquiry submission must show and confirm the selected recipient and shared fields.

Outside contact remains supported after this gate. Provider identity can still be searched on social media; portfolio watermarks, descriptions, websites or social links may reveal numbers. Define a reasonable listing/contact-link policy without promising perfect containment or adding a large OCR project. Do not suppress truthful business identity/reviews to make the gate work.

## Repeat-use proposal and scope

1. Start with saved providers and a usable contact/enquiry history. Let people distinguish contacted, awaiting response and their own reported choice without pretending to confirm outside negotiations.
2. Offer an optional occasion workspace showing service needs and missing categories. A person who found catering may still need photography or decoration. Reuse explicitly supplied locality/date/party-size information; budgets remain service-specific. Saving a photographer is not consent to contact caterers.
3. Deliver requested service updates and optional reminders with truthful triggers. Marketing and cross-occasion promotions require separate consent and withdrawal. Avoid unsolicited funeral reminders or inferred personal occasions.
4. Let customers return for a new event and deliberately copy relevant saved details, updating date, budget and privacy choices. Multi-person planning/invitations are a later proposal needing explicit ownership/access design; do not add them to the current build merely because competitors have collaboration.
5. Give providers useful demand reports and response tools. Separate profile views, distinct contact actions, structured enquiries and source-labelled reported hires. Subscription renewal needs evidence of value, not just a larger registered-user count.

These features are selected hypotheses, not measured Ghanaian preferences or a mandate to build a full event-planning suite before validating discovery. Keep all occasion families supported; learn which organising groups actually recur.

## Measurement and validation

Measure completed eligible contact actions per eligible contact intent alongside signup/verification completion and drop-off. Keep windows, deduplication and eligible population defined. Use customer/provider follow-up, where consented, to distinguish attempted contact from a genuine two-way conversation. Unreported outcomes remain unknown rather than failures or successes.

Track return for another service within the same event, return for a later event, enquiry acknowledgement and provider paid renewal separately. Segment first-time organisers from people sourcing services repeatedly; do not invent their frequency. CEREMO does not observe service GMV through checkout and must not fabricate it. A contact gate is unsuccessful if registration improves while useful provider connections materially deteriorate.

Begin with observed Greater Accra organiser/provider tasks and verification usability, including mobile data and interrupted flows. For a later sufficiently powered experiment, predefine outcome/guardrail metrics, assignment, exposure, duration and analysis; avoid only comparing the self-selected users who registered. Small-pilot counts support qualitative decisions, not a population-wide uplift claim. Numeric thresholds, quotas and universal test duration remain unset.

## Current source and reuse

Read current [AccountService](../../../src/main/java/io/ceremo/ceremobackend/account/application/AccountService.java): requireActiveAccount loads the persisted account and denies non-ACTIVE status. [Accounts](../../../src/main/java/io/ceremo/ceremobackend/account/application/port/in/Accounts.java) exposes this reusable boundary. Retain trusted Keycloak verification rather than accepting client-supplied verified/status fields. Read the existing [security configuration](../../../src/main/java/io/ceremo/ceremobackend/shared/authentication/infrastructure/primary/SecurityConfiguration.java): specified provider/profile/catalogue GETs are public; other API routes require authentication. Public route permission does not imply contacts must be public or that the planned controllers exist.

Shared: reuse existing identity, errors/assertions and central JWT security. Wire: reuse existing security/CORS and account composition. Proposed gap: a protected provider contact use case and response, plus deliberate public-profile field exclusion and bounded abuse controls. Public provider DTO/HTML/JSON-LD must not contain gated phone/email/wa.me/tel destinations. Contact responses must not enter shared public caches or logs. Appropriate per-account/network abuse limits need an approved operating policy; account creation alone does not stop scraping. No new duplicate identity store, arbitrary timer, payment feature or authentication helper is justified.

Initial research stage only: no production code, migration, test, dependency, configuration, coverage rule or Sonar result changed then. The later authorised implementation is recorded below.

## Original coordinated documentation proposal

After the contact policy/first implementation scope is agreed, update existing documents 01–07 and 09 where affected: evidence, access rules, HTTP/DTO contract, journey, contact-button states, minimal contact-action data and build tasks. Document 08 should then specify meaningful gate/response-leak/denied-account tests. Update related agent memory so older public-contact snippets are not treated as the current implementation specification. No extra public product document is needed. A contact-gate proposal must not silently introduce a full chat service, phone OTP or call recording.

Verification: source/document review and cited public-page retrieval only. No local interviews or causal conversion evidence exists for this change. ## Applied registered-profile boundary, 5 November 2026

Approval: the founder accepted the recommendation and required registration before opening a provider/tenant profile or sensitive details. Interpretation stated before edits: tenant means provider business; customer-facing profile access differs from private business workspace access. Anonymous users retain catalogue and limited-summary search. Full profiles, detailed reviews and contact destinations require authentication plus a persisted ACTIVE local account. Private tenants remain restricted to accepted members and operation-specific ownership/role checks; an unrelated administrator has no blanket member-read permission. No new REGISTERED role or membership from JWT organisation claims is introduced.

### Maintainer evidence and adaptations

- [Spring request authorisation](https://docs.spring.io/spring-security/reference/servlet/authorization/authorize-http-requests.html), manual 7.1.2, explains custom request access managers and ordered matchers. CEREMO runs Security 7.1.1, so actual [RequestMatcherDelegatingAuthorizationManager source](https://github.com/spring-projects/spring-security/blob/7.1.1/web/src/main/java/org/springframework/security/web/access/intercept/RequestMatcherDelegatingAuthorizationManager.java) was also read. Its delegation includes the short excerpt `return manager.authorize(authentication,`; the first matching rule controls the request.
- Actual [AuthenticatedAuthorizationManager 7.1.1](https://github.com/spring-projects/spring-security/blob/7.1.1/core/src/main/java/org/springframework/security/authorization/AuthenticatedAuthorizationManager.java), authorize and authenticated methods, delegates authentication classification to Spring's trust resolver. Reuse it so anonymous tokens are not accepted merely because their isAuthenticated flag is true.
- Source licences: Apache-2.0. The adapter is original CEREMO policy code calling existing library APIs; no external source/dependency was imported. Pinned upstream test URLs for both managers returned cache misses through the browsing tool; those tests were not claimed as inspected. Current local tests verify the adaptation instead. [OWASP API3](https://api-security.owasp.org/editions/2023/en/0xa3-broken-object-property-level-authorization/) remains the response-property safeguard; property leakage tests for actual marketplace DTOs await implementation.

### Actual changes and reuse

[ActiveAccountAuthorizationManager](../../../src/main/java/io/ceremo/ceremobackend/account/infrastructure/primary/security/ActiveAccountAuthorizationManager.java) lives in the outer account HTTP adapter. Spring checks authentication before local account storage. The existing Accounts.requireActiveAccount supplies the lifecycle rule. Only known missing-account/restricted-account failures become a denied decision; unexpected failures propagate without a grant. Plain account/tenant domain and application layers remain framework-independent.

[Shared SecurityConfiguration](../../../src/main/java/io/ceremo/ceremobackend/shared/authentication/infrastructure/primary/SecurityConfiguration.java) injects the existing Accounts bean, removes detail/review paths from the anonymous GET list and gates provider detail paths/subroutes. Catalogues, safe summary GET and health checks retain their specific allowlist. No extra chain, wire bean, runtime dependency, migration or local identity store was created. Existing account registration/activation and logout paths remain reachable under their existing authentication rules.

[TenantService](../../../src/main/java/io/ceremo/ceremobackend/tenant/application/TenantService.java) already enforces ACTIVE account, accepted membership, owner-only team operations and recent-MFA staff administration. These rules were retained. Registration must never replace private ownership/membership with a simple hasRole check. Planned provider settings, billing, evidence and media need their own use-case/record permissions, even behind the new generic route gate.

Updated the nine existing public documents, README, agent rules, maps and reuse guidance. ADR 11.10 supersedes the public-profile/contact requirement. Proposed nullable contact_action user IDs remain compatible with minimisation/erasure, but can never authorise guest contact. Public summaries omit full profile content, contact URLs, private tenant identifiers/team/owner, billing and evidence. Media and caches must respect the same distinctions when provider features are built.

### Tests and remaining scope

Focused account authorisation/security-chain/tenant wiring/architecture command passed: `.\gradlew.bat test --tests '*ActiveAccountAuthorizationManagerTest' --tests '*SecurityConfigurationTest' --tests '*TenantSecurityWiringTest' --tests '*AccountArchitectureTest' --console=plain`.

New checks cover anonymous/null/unauthenticated identities without storage access; known denied accounts; unexpected failures without grants; bearer versus browser-session separation; real signed tokens with no local account/PENDING/ACTIVE/SUSPENDED/ANONYMISED; an unrelated registered customer or admin denied private tenant records. Test-only provider handlers establish route protection and do not implement a provider marketplace. Existing tenant isolation, consent, rollback and concurrency tests remain required. Full-build/coverage results belong in the [quality register](../quality/tests-and-analysis.md).

Final verification: `.\gradlew.bat check bootJar --console=plain` passed; 532 regular and 50 PostgreSQL tests, zero failures/errors/skips. Combined coverage: 2155 lines and 449 branches covered, none missed per application class. JAR inspection confirms the guard is packaged and the provider fixture is not. See the [fresh quality checkpoint](../quality/tests-and-analysis.md#registered-profile-access-5-november-2026).

Provider publication/entitlement, safe production summary/detail DTOs, protected media, contact-action persistence/rate limits, frontend return-state integration and actual retention features remain feature work. Live Keycloak/SMTP/MFA, Sonar server gate and remote CI remain separate checks. Documentation version 3.4, reviewed locally with humanizer guidance; Grammarly unavailable/pending. No company text uploaded, no live realm or business records changed, no retention uplift or production-readiness claim.
